experiments.title: Was the method-vs-baseline comparison FAIR (matched budget, matched search budget, the paper's own setup)?
experiments.goal: Audit comparison fairness
experiments.comparison: Budget, tuning allocation, augmentation, and paper configuration
experiments.why: Find unresolved denominator mismatches
experiments.result: Every registered fairness flaw is closed: budget and search budget (CORRECTIONS 30/44) and the parent's unaugmented setup on both datasets, where tuned SGD+momentum+cosine still beats the method by +3.6173 pp (CIFAR-10, cau1) and +12.1780 pp (CIFAR-100, cuc1).
experiments.reason: Goal met: the deficit is not an artefact of the three audited unfairnesses (MASTER-TABLE row 19 moved OPEN -> CONFIRMED, RESCOPED at CORRECTIONS 229).
experiments.scope: Limits that travel with the verdict: one baseline family (SGD+momentum+cosine); the paper's alpha0 1e-6 is untested on CIFAR-100 (on CIFAR-10 the paper's config m6 is 15.1160 pp behind); one granularity per batch, so meta-side tuning is bounded, not exhausted (cuc1's best cell sits at the ms-HIGH grid edge, +0.28 SE above the centre). No method-side counterweight, ResNet18 only, 100 epochs only, and the AUC reading reverses at the best baseline rung on both datasets.

experiments.comparison: Seven SGD rates versus two MetaOptimize initializations
experiments.why: Address the parent-paper augmentation objection
experiments.result: Unaugmented SGD beats the better registered meta cell by 3.617 pp.
experiments.reason: The registered CIFAR-10 deficit survives without augmentation.
experiments.scope: CAU1, n=3 fresh seeds per arm, one batch, 100 epochs; ingest uncommitted. Amended at CORRECTIONS 229: Outcome unchanged (DEFICIT-HOLDS on CIFAR-10). This batch's own method side is still two alpha0 cells at one meta-stepsize.

experiments.title: Is N_eff/m stationary in training time, or is the headline a 20-epoch sentence?
experiments.goal: Preserve effective independence in later training windows
experiments.comparison: Epochs 10–20 vs 20–40 at each granularity
experiments.why: Check whether early measurements describe later training.
experiments.result: Nodewise and weightwise decline; layerwise change remains unresolved.
experiments.reason: The effective-independence fraction changes substantially in the finer partitions.
experiments.scope: R18/C10; br6 n=4 per rung, all 12 seeds box-free. Changes are -0.0359/-0.1260/-0.3556 for layer/node/weight. Layerwise is a resolution-limited bound, not evidence of stationarity. No budget-coupled schedule exists: this is a window/time contrast, not an independent causal budget intervention.

experiments.title: Is N_eff/m an artefact of the BETA_CLIP guard box every run sits inside?
experiments.goal: Keep effective-independence measurements robust to guard changes
experiments.comparison: Published guard boxes vs measured box-free configurations
experiments.why: Test whether clipping creates the measurement headline.
experiments.result: Box removal changes N_eff/m only −0.006 to +0.024 across four families.
experiments.reason: All shifts stay within the registered measurement tolerance.
experiments.scope: 20 epochs; tested configurations only. Box-free family fractions: R10 .1571, R18 .5045, R34 .5474, C100 .3124. R18 four-box span .076 against historical .10 tolerance. Do not generalize the row's '+.027 pp accuracy-neutral' aside: fa1 and later audits show accuracy effects depend on recipe, bound and horizon.

experiments.title: Is a step-size adapter a HIGH-PASS FILTER on meta-gradient correlation — and is it a dial or a switch?
experiments.goal: Test gradual adaptation of the correlation profile
experiments.comparison: Frozen beta vs two valid meta-step settings
experiments.why: Distinguish a gradual response from a switch.
experiments.result: N_eff/m rises 0.042 → 0.129 → 0.481 as meta-step increases.
experiments.reason: The intermediate setting lands between the two endpoint profiles.
experiments.scope: R18/C10, ml5, 20 epochs, n=3 per rung. Profile exponent .343→.219→.081 and k=1 suppression 1→3.37→21.09. The ms=1e-2 rung is guard-dominated and excluded from this conclusion. 'High-pass' describes scale-selective measured suppression, not an established causal theory of optimization.

experiments.title: Off the meta-optimum, does the correlation have a RANGE (short-range, channel-scaled) or is the falling profile an estimator artefact?
experiments.goal: Verify short-range correlation beyond estimator artifacts
experiments.comparison: Corrected scale profiles vs exchangeable and independence models
experiments.why: Remove heterogeneity before interpreting the profile.
experiments.result: Frozen-beta profiles fall 16.6–264.6× across the four tested families.
experiments.reason: The falling profiles survive the corrected independence floor.
experiments.scope: Off-equilibrium/frozen beta, 20 epochs, n=2 per arm. rho_w is an implied sign-correlation parameter, not marginal-sign E(u). Steady R18 corrected span69.3 versus uncorrected165.5. Free-beta profiles flatten; R10 free exchangeability is undecided at7.8× rather than universally accepted. Do not call the shape dataset- or architecture-independent beyond these four combinations.

experiments.title: Can a box-free (guard-free) configuration exist at this budget? — an extrapolation used as a design premise
experiments.goal: Predict future guard contact from current velocity
experiments.comparison: Projected guard contact vs the observed continuation
experiments.why: Test whether measured velocity supports extrapolation.
experiments.result: One seed reaccelerates; contact occurs 12.4 epochs earlier than predicted.
experiments.reason: A declining observed velocity did not remain declining.
experiments.scope: Startup forecasts: 0/5 “will bind” and 5/5 “will not bind” predictions correct. A later projection gave 22.8 extra epochs, but contact occurred after 10.4; one seed’s v/vmax rose .123 → .379. The contact happened earlier, so the forecast was not conservative.

experiments.why: Test whether matched depth alone suffices
experiments.result: Carrier isolation beats the matched triple by 46.5233 pp; magnitude remains confounded.
experiments.reason: Matched non-carriers fail to rescue under the registered identity test.
experiments.scope: cdep1, 18 runs, 100 ep, CIFAR-100/ResNet18_c100, ONE batch, FRESH seeds {24,25,26}; ingest 2,761 → 2,779 (added 18, changed 0, removed 0); 16.05 GPU-h, re-summed here over its own 18 wallclock_min values (minute-rounded, so marginally below sacct) Amended at CORRECTIONS 229: Outcome unchanged (IDENTITY-OPERATIVE holds). 'ResNet-only' is rescoped to this batch's DEPTH control: the nominated set rescuing where a matched non-carrier set does not has since been measured on VGG (cvi1), GroupNorm (cgn2) and PlainNet (cpl2). The tensor list does not transfer, and identity vs magnitude is still not separated on any network.

experiments.title: POST-HOC SYNTHESIS — the audit's headline. At a fixed group count, does the uniform partition beat the architecture-aligned one in every count-matched cell, and by how much?
experiments.goal: POST-HOC SYNTHESIS — the audit's headline. At a fixed group count, does the uniform partition beat the architecture-aligned one in every count-matched cell, and by how much?
experiments.comparison: uniform chunk<K> minus architecture-aligned nodewise, count-matched (R18 14,421 v 14,420; R34 25,562 v 25,556; C100 14,595 v 14,600), ONE batch per cell; across cells: network (R18 / R34 / R50), dataset (C10 / C100), base (SGDm / SGD / RMSProp / AdamW), meta (Lion; RMSProp in sm4 only), ms (1e-4 / 3e-4), budget (100 / 300 ep), three boxes
experiments.why: Count-matched partition audit (MASTER-TABLE section 10): does the partition matter once the group count is held fixed?
experiments.result: D > 0 in 20 of 20 cells; t ≥ 3.0 in 18 (the two below are ml2 t 2.34 and sm3 t 2.22); D runs from +0.141 (sm3) to +1.640 (gc1). Eight SGDm cells (cc1, mm1, pp1, gn1-BN, rl3 ×2, fa1, hz3): fixed-effect pool +0.5556 ± 0.0448, Q 4.21 on 7 df, τ 0. Fourteen byte-identical-contrast cells: +0.5297 ± 0.0294, Q 102.47 on 13 df, τ 0.2948. TRAIN agrees in sign in 20 of 20. The simulation-calibrated 95 % half-width ±0.121 and the SGDm null median 9.4 are NOT re-derived by the independent parser; analysis/c98_reproduce.py, run unedited, reproduces both (PASS), although that audit exits 1 on ten stale corpus-count checks.
experiments.reason: Verdict: "wins all twenty count-matched cells" (MAIN-IDEA-REPORT §5 and the paper's abstract; a pool no scorer registered a bar for, paper §3.4) Goal met: Registered headline claim: uniform beats aligned in 20 of 20 count-matched cells. A synthesis; runs link on the per-batch rows.
experiments.scope: the 20 cells of the paper's Table 2 (analysis/c98_figures.py CELLS, the gn1-GroupNorm cell excluded): 18 batches, 154 runs, n 3 v 3 to 9 v 9. The partition matters at fixed count, by about 0.6 pp — small next to the method's own deficit against tuned SGD: −1.807 pp as published and −1.796 as c98_reproduce.py now derives it on CIFAR-10, −5.699 pp on CIFAR-100 (cdn1), outside the "1.8–4.2 pp" MAIN-IDEA-REPORT quotes. Six of the twenty cells come from the five batches with no scorer registered before their runs (ml2, nl1 ×2, r50, gm2, sm3), and two of those (ml2, sm3) were VOID on their registered meta axis and enter as Lion replicates. The effect is heterogeneous across base optimisers (the moderator row).

experiments.goal: Is the weightwise accuracy deficit at its own tuned meta-stepsize a box (clamp) artefact — and where does the fully tuned granularity ladder peak?

experiments.result: plateau5 layerwise 92.939, nodewise 91.961, weightwise 91.234 (n=3 each). T1: weightwise box-free on 3/3 seeds, and every arm 0.0000 on all four occupancy columns (quoted, 104.2). With the 13-axis census the tuned ladder reads frozen 90.384 → scalar 92.262 → blk6 92.652 → layerwise 92.887 → nodewise 92.450 → weightwise 91.146, an interior optimum at layerwise (quoted, 104.4). experiments.reason: Verdict: T1 CONFIRMS + T4 DECIDED Goal met: T1 CONFIRMS and T4 DECIDED: the weightwise deficit is not a clamp artefact.

experiments.goal: At (nearly) fixed group count, does the PARTITION matter — is granularity one variable (m) or two (count, partition)?

experiments.why: Count-matched partition audit (MASTER-TABLE section 10): does the partition matter once the group count is held fixed?
experiments.result: chunk1024 92.526 vs tw0 nodewise 91.961: +0.565 pp, se 0.089, t 6.38 (cross-batch, and 24 % apart in m). Post-hoc decomposition: count +0.049, partition +0.517 (quoted, 105.3). K1: chunk1 − tw0 weightwise = −0.255, se 0.146, t −1.74, inside ±0.50.
experiments.reason: Verdict: K1 REPRODUCES + K2 REFUTES Mixed: K1 REPRODUCES; K2 REFUTES its own registered prediction that the partition does not matter at fixed m. Judgement call: the row's question was answered yes.
experiments.scope: ck1, 15 runs (chunk K ∈ {1, 2, 16, 128, 1024} × 3 seeds), R18/C10, SGDm+Lion, ms 1e-4, 100 ep, read against tw0 (CROSS-batch). K2 refuted its own registered prediction that the partition does not matter at fixed m, which made the axis (count, partition) and opened this audit. It had been registered as the more interesting outcome, with a symmetric ±0.50 bar. Not yet an alignment claim: at matched m the two partitions still differ in size distribution (105.3). mm1 re-measured it at matched count.

experiments.title: Does the partition effect survive a MEASURED matched-count contrast rather than an interpolated, cross-batch one?
experiments.goal: Does the partition effect survive a MEASURED matched-count contrast rather than an interpolated, cross-batch one?
experiments.comparison: chunk777 (m 14,421) vs nodewise (m 14,420), one batch, one ms
experiments.why: Count-matched partition audit (MASTER-TABLE section 10): does the partition matter once the group count is held fixed?
experiments.result: 92.529 vs 92.044: D = +0.485, se 0.161, t 3.01; TRAIN D +0.437. M2: mm1 nodewise − tw0 nodewise = +0.083 — with ck1's −0.255, a cross-batch offset with no stable sign.
experiments.reason: Verdict: M1 CONFIRMS + M2 REPRODUCES Goal met: M1 CONFIRMS the first measured count-matched D; M2 REPRODUCES.
experiments.scope: mm1, 6 runs, R18/C10, SGDm+Lion, ms 1e-4, box -15:-2.3026, 100 ep, seeds 0–2. The first measured count-matched D. It cleared the pre-registered UNDECIDED band (+0.15, +0.30] by ONE standard error at n=3, which 106.2 says; M2 was declared unable to void M1 before the data existed. Nineteen more cells have since matched it (first row).

experiments.title: Which property of the partition carries D — architecture ALIGNMENT, or the group-SIZE distribution?
experiments.goal: Which property of the partition carries D — architecture ALIGNMENT, or the group-SIZE distribution?
experiments.comparison: nodewise vs permnode<S> (nodewise's exact count and per-tensor size multiset, membership randomised WITHIN each tensor) vs chunk777, one batch
experiments.why: Count-matched partition audit (MASTER-TABLE section 10): does the partition matter once the group count is held fixed?
experiments.result: A = permnode − nodewise = −0.009, se 0.157, t −0.06 (alignment); B = chunk777 − permnode = +0.590, se 0.107, t 5.53 (size distribution, about all of D); D = +0.581, se 0.141, t 4.11. 66.64 % of nodewise's 14,420 groups are size 1 — the 41 BatchNorm scale/shift and linear.bias tensors, 9,610 scalars on 0.09 % of the weights (quoted, 107.4).
experiments.reason: Verdict: P2 NULL + P1 REPLICATES Mixed: P1 REPLICATES the size-distribution effect; P2 is a bounded NULL on alignment, not a refutation.
experiments.scope: pp1, 9 runs, R18/C10, ms 1e-4, 100 ep, seeds 0–2 (the permutation seed IS the run seed). The rival the literature would assume, alignment, is a NULL — a bounded null, not a refutation: its 95 % CI [−0.317, +0.298] spans −55 % to +51 % of D and the NULL band (±0.15) was narrower than the realised se, so "ALIGNMENT IS REFUTED" may not be written (125.1, 126.1). The permutation is within-tensor only, so it is silent on layer boundaries. rp1 replicated it at twice the power.

experiments.title: The degenerate-tail test: with only the 9,610 size-1 groups merged away, does the matched-count gap collapse?
experiments.goal: The degenerate-tail test: with only the 9,610 size-1 groups merged away, does the matched-count gap collapse?
experiments.comparison: nodewise1d (nodewise on every tensor with ndim ≥ 2, ONE group per 1-D tensor) vs chunk2325, m 4,851 EXACTLY; nodewise anchor
experiments.why: Count-matched partition audit (MASTER-TABLE section 10): does the partition matter once the group count is held fixed?
experiments.result: G = chunk2325 − nodewise1d = +0.295, se 0.048, t 6.15 — inside the band (+0.15, +0.30] registered UNDECIDED, 0.005 pp short of SURVIVES. T = nodewise1d − nodewise = +0.427, t 10.43, count-confounded (14,420 → 4,851). T3: nodewise 92.184 reproduces mm1 and pp1.
experiments.reason: Verdict: T1 UNDECIDED + T2 CONFIRMS + T3 REPRODUCES + T5 NOT APPLICABLE Open: The primary tail test T1 is UNDECIDED (0.005 pp short of SURVIVES); T2 and T3 are secondary.
experiments.scope: bn1, 9 runs, R18/C10, ms 1e-4, 100 ep, seeds 0–2. The bands were not moved and no seeds were added after seeing which side it fell on (108.6a). T2 was registered as count-confounded before submission and is not evidence about the tail. Later SGDm cells put G near zero (cc1 +0.011, fa1 −0.001, rl3@1e-4 −0.011), but bn1's T1 stays UNDECIDED.

experiments.goal: Is D an argmax artefact (every D so far read at ms 1e-4, 0.42 pp below nodewise's better stepsize)? And with the tail removed, does the gap collapse?
experiments.comparison: {nodewise, chunk777, nodewise1d, chunk2325} at ms 3e-4
experiments.why: Count-matched partition audit (MASTER-TABLE section 10): does the partition matter once the group count is held fixed?
experiments.reason: Verdict: A1 SURVIVES + A2 COLLAPSES + A3 VOID Open: A3 VOID: 0 of 12 arms box-free, and the cell was removed from the primaries.
experiments.scope: ar1, 12 runs, R18/C10, box -15:-2.3026, 100 ep, seeds 0–2. At the time, "the gap lives entirely in the size-1 tail". Later removed from the primaries: the corrected occupancy instrument (117.1) finds ar1 floor-bound asymmetrically — nodewise 0.110 vs chunk777 0.0014 of coordinates, 75× — and the floor holds nodewise's step sizes UP, which inflates D; ar1 is box-VOID and is not among the twenty cells. fa1 re-read the same cell with a floor that cannot bind.

correction.note: A1 SURVIVES and A2 COLLAPSES were later removed from the primaries: the corrected occupancy instrument (CORRECTIONS 117.1) finds ar1 floor-bound.

experiments.title: Direction C — does the meta-gradient sign-agreement field (N_eff/m) predict accuracy at matched count? The pre-registered test that decides it.
experiments.goal: Direction C — does the meta-gradient sign-agreement field (N_eff/m) predict accuracy at matched count? The pre-registered test that decides it.
experiments.comparison: {nodewise, chunk777, nodewise1d, chunk2325} at the only stepsize where the field is readable (ms 1e-4), fresh seeds
experiments.why: Count-matched partition audit (MASTER-TABLE section 10): does the partition matter once the group count is held fixed?
experiments.result: C2 contrast: accuracy +0.727 (t +3.63) against d(N_eff/m) −0.0237 (t −11.14), ANTI-CONCORDANT. C3 contrast: accuracy +0.011 (t +0.08) against −0.0529 (t −23.26), DISSOCIATION (field numbers quoted, 110.2; accuracy re-derived).
experiments.reason: Verdict: C1 MIXED → direction C IS DROPPED Goal missed: C1 MIXED, so direction C IS DROPPED: the field does not predict accuracy at matched count (as for MT098).
experiments.scope: cc1, 12 runs, R18/C10, 100 ep, seeds 3–5; 12/12 box-free, rec_lo = rec_hi = 0.0000 (quoted). The field resolves at t −11 and −23 and is decisively wrong about accuracy on one contrast and silent on the other: the correlation statistic the Adam-mini / Adalayer / SGG line would reach for does not track the outcome. This is mechanism M2, refuted on a gate registered before its data. A second VOID had been costed as DROP in advance, so this cannot be reread as "try again".

experiments.goal: The ms/box deconfound: re-read ar1's cell with a floor that cannot bind — does the box change the optimiser, and do D and G survive in a free box?

experiments.why: Count-matched partition audit (MASTER-TABLE section 10): does the partition matter once the group count is held fixed?
experiments.result: F3, fa1 − ar1 per arm: nodewise −0.020 (t −0.15), chunk777 −0.088 (t −0.83), nodewise1d −0.177 (t −2.22), chunk2325 −0.039 (t −0.57). F2: D_w = +0.629, se 0.123, t 5.11; G_w = −0.001, se 0.076, t −0.01. Floor free on 24/24; the ceiling binds on the nodewise arm on 5 of 6 seeds under the corrected instrument (both quoted, 113, 117.1).
experiments.reason: Verdict: F3 THE BOX CHANGED THE OPTIMISER, NOT MERELY THE INSTRUMENT. + F2 SURVIVES + G_w CONSISTENT-WITH-BOX-FREE (UNDERPOWERED) + F1 DISSOCIATION Mixed: F2 SURVIVES, but F3 defied its registered expectation (the box changed the optimiser) and G_w is underpowered.
experiments.scope: fa1, 24 runs in two waves of 12, R18/C10, 100 ep, seeds 0–5. The tail story survives without gaining a replication. It is the corpus's first box-free ms 3e-4 cell and one of the eight SGDm cells, and it produced STANDING RULE 14 (seed labels do not pair across batches).

experiments.title: Do degenerate size-1 groups CAUSE the parent paper's granularity non-monotonicity — are size-1 groups the carrier as a general size law (mechanism M3)?
experiments.goal: Do degenerate size-1 groups CAUSE the parent paper's granularity non-monotonicity — are size-1 groups the carrier as a general size law (mechanism M3)?
experiments.comparison: four checks on runs already on disk: the parent's own text, its §9 clause, layerwise → nodewise at the parent's η 1e-3 in five batches, and ck1's chunk1 (100 % singletons) → chunk2 (0 %)
experiments.why: Count-matched partition audit (MASTER-TABLE section 10): does the partition matter once the group count is held fixed?
experiments.result: K4: chunk1 90.979 → chunk2 91.095, +0.115, se 0.133, t 0.87, against a count-only prediction of +0.131 to +0.161 — removing every singleton buys nothing, and the ladder has no kink where f collapses. K3: at η 1e-3 the 66.6 %-singleton partition WINS by +0.76 to +1.25 pp in 5 of 5 batches (quoted, 119.0).
experiments.reason: Verdict: "REFUTED" (CORRECTIONS 119.0: "Size-1 groups cause the non-monotonicity" is REFUTED; the paper's M3) Goal missed: REFUTED: size-1 groups do not cause the non-monotonicity (CORRECTIONS 119.0).
experiments.scope: zero GPU; ck1 in-batch; br6, bl5, bf8, bf9, sp8. What survives is narrower and better measured: shattering the 41 one-dimensional normalisation tensors while the weights they scale stay grouped costs 0.43–0.82 pp at matched count — an architectural prescription, not a size law and not a variance law. "Variance" as the mechanism is struck too.

experiments.result: PRIMARY D = plateau5(kL) - plateau5(k01) = 51.8173 - 14.4340 = +37.3833 pp = +63.08 SE (SE 0.5927; the in-batch sigma 0.7259 dominates the frozen prior 0.5862). TRAIN 60.5467 vs 16.5167, D(TRAIN) +44.0300. Seeds k01 14.236 / 14.380 / 14.686, kL 52.200 / 50.682 / 52.570. D >= 23.274 -> FULL-SIZE; D_rel 0.4369 against the BN in-batch median 0.6045 (descriptive). Account (B) (abs D <= 2) refuted; (A)'s D band hit, both of (A)'s levels missed LOW. Two bounds: the scalar beta never reaches the -15 clamp inside 100 epochs (0 of 500 records on every seed; it ends at -12.30 / -11.78 / -11.55), and kL is still rising at +0.29 to +0.34 pp/epoch over epochs 80-99 (epoch-to-epoch jitter 1.5-3.0 pp), so D is a 100-epoch snapshot, not a converged gap. experiments.reason: Verdict: GAP-REPLICATES + HARNESS-CLEAN + FULL-SIZE + SIGMA-INBATCH-DOMINATES + TRAIN-AGREES + K01-BELOW-BN-FLOOR-BAND + GN32-ALSO-CHANGES-PER-CHANNEL-INVARIANCE + HORIZON-100-ONLY + PROBE-RECORDS-PRESENT Goal met: GAP-REPLICATES and FULL-SIZE: the scalar-to-layerwise gap exists on GroupNorm ResNet-18 (a 100-epoch snapshot).

experiments.title: Once ResNet-18's residual additions are removed, and nothing else, do the surviving ex-carrier BN scales still carry the gap -- the one-variable test of 189.2's residual account?
experiments.goal: Once ResNet-18's residual additions are removed, and nothing else, do the surviving ex-carrier BN scales still carry the gap -- the one-variable test of 189.2's residual account?
experiments.comparison: PlainNet18_c100 = ResNet18_c100 with every out += shortcut(x) removed and the 3 projection shortcuts not constructed (53 tensors): k01, kL, ISO {layer4.0.bn2.weight, layer4.1.bn2.weight} [51,2], its exact bn1 twin CTL {layer4.0.bn1.weight, layer4.1.bn1.weight} [51,2], ONE {layer4.0.bn2.weight} [52,1]; ONE batch
experiments.why: Mechanism-hunt row in section 9's convention, appended at the file's end so that no existing line moves -- CORRECTIONS 218.
experiments.result: PRIMARY DELTA_ID = ISO - CTL = 67.5427 - 11.6967 = +55.8460 pp = +98.49 SE; KEY D_ONE = ONE - k01 = 11.6840 - 11.7867 = -0.1027 pp = -0.18 SE; D_GAP +57.1933 (kL 68.9800); RECOVERY 0.9749, RECOVERY_ONE -0.0018 (ResNet's ONE ~0.91, between-batch). TRAIN: k01 11.80, kL 97.65, ISO 82.36, CTL 11.71, ONE 11.79; DELTA_ID(TRAIN) +70.65. SE 0.5670 (the frozen prior; in-batch 0.2218). On k01's own pinned records layer4.1.bn2.weight holds 0.6201 of the mass and removing it flips the remainder sign on 1.0000 (non-gating). Two bounds: k01 floors at 11.79, below every collapse account's registered 20-36; and ISO's rescue is a DELAY -- its complement group pins at the clamp at epoch 60-62 (k01's at 36), so ISO's level is frozen and matches kL on TEST (-1.44 pp) but not on TRAIN (-15.29 pp). Registered scorer run UNEDITED on alice2, exit 0; an independent parser agrees digit for digit.
experiments.reason: Verdict: HEAD-CARRIES-PLAIN + GATES-CLEAN + ONE-VARIABLE-RESIDUAL-ABLATION + THIRD-CARRIER-ABSENT + MAGNITUDE-NOT-SEPARATED + MISTUNING-NOT-EXCLUDED + HORIZON-100-ONLY + SIGMA-PRIOR-FROZEN + H-BROKEN-EXCLUDED + FLOOR-READINGS-ARE-BOUNDS + DECOMPOSITION-BY-SUBTRACTION + TRAIN-AGREES + ISO-TRACKS-KL + CTL-AT-FLOOR + ONE-AT-FLOOR Mixed: HEAD-CARRIES-PLAIN: ISO rescues against its twin, but ONE stays at the floor and 189.2's literal forms missed their registered branches.
experiments.scope: cpl1, 15 runs, PlainNet18_c100 / CIFAR-100, SGDm+Lion, ms 1e-3, α₀ 1e-6, box -15:-2.3026, AUGMENT=1, 100 ep, fresh seeds {69,70,71}; ingested with cgn1 (2,863 -> 2,884, added 21, changed 0); 9.82 GPU-h re-summed over its own 15 wallclock_min values (sacct 9.95). One-variable support for 189.2 for layer4.0.bn2.weight ONLY: removing the addition it fed removed its carrier status, and ISO's in-batch rescue kills H-BROKEN, so ONE's null is real. And 189.2 as a characterisation of WHICH tensors carry does not survive: its two literal forms (R-ONLY, R-NOGAP) missed their registered branches -- a rescue exists with no addition anywhere, and by subtraction it rides on layer4.1.bn2.weight, a summand of nothing, as PATH (a conv-free path to the classifier) predicted. NOT licensed: layer4.1.bn2.weight as a measured carrier (never isolated alone); identity vs magnitude; anything about layer4.0.shortcut.1.weight (absent); PATH as confirmed (its k01 level missed); any horizon but 100 epochs; RULE 11. Amended at CORRECTIONS 229: Outcome unchanged (Mixed). 'By subtraction' and 'never isolated alone' are overtaken by cpl2 (MT217): layer4.1.bn2.weight alone rescues (+52.1367 pp over its twin). 'Alone' holds only against the bar (ISO minus HEAD is +3.5940 pp inside the 5.0 pp bar), HEAD's rescue is a delay, and identity vs magnitude is still open. Amended at CORRECTIONS 231: Outcome unchanged (Mixed). cvt1 landed at CORRECTIONS 230 as MT218 (STEP-SIZE-NEEDED-VOTE-SUFFICES): silencing layer4.1.bn2.weight's term in the shared meta-gradient sum while it keeps the shared step size does not rescue (MUTE 10.9860 vs k01 11.9493; the DOWN vote is re-carried by 47, 44, 41 and 38), isolating it does (HEAD 64.7940), and its bn1 twin's term x691 inside HEAD's complement re-pins that complement at epoch 37.6 and drops the arm to 30.1400 (0.344 of the gap kept). Its rescue needs its own step size; magnitude is still not separated from identity in level. Amended at CORRECTIONS 236: Outcome unchanged (Mixed). Row 213's CORRECTIONS 231 update said a carrier-sized vote collapses a complement 'whoever casts it'. That claimed more than was tested and was corrected in place: one other caster (layer4.1.bn1.weight) was run, into one complement (HEAD's), at one K in cvt1 (MT218) and at five K in cvt2 (MT221); whether any other tensor's term does the same is untested. The superseded wording stays in the row.

experiments.title: Does the VGG isolation rescue survive a LONG horizon, or is cvi1's +31.28 pp a 100-epoch artefact of a complement that had not yet pinned?
experiments.goal: Does the VGG isolation rescue survive a LONG horizon, or is cvi1's +31.28 pp a 100-epoch artefact of a complement that had not yet pinned?
experiments.comparison: horizon alone: the four cvi1 arms, spec strings BYTE-IDENTICAL to cvi1's, run to 328 epochs with the 100-epoch control read IN-RUN from the same runs (SCHED=none, so num_epochs is only the loop bound); k01 scalar floor, kL layerwise ceiling, ISO sets:1-22,24-26/bn8.weight [25,1], CTL sets:1-19,21-26/bn7.weight [25,1]; ONE batch
experiments.why: Mechanism-hunt row in section 9's convention, appended at the file's end so that no existing line moves -- CORRECTIONS 219.
experiments.result: PRIMARY RHO = D_ISO@328 / D_ISO@100 = +32.0093 / +32.0053 = 1.0001, both IN BATCH, D_ISO = plateau5(ISO) - plateau5(k01); +42.36 SE and +42.35 SE on SE 0.755682 (the frozen sigma 0.925518 dominates the in-batch 0.244624, df 16). Levels TEST @100 -> @328: k01 35.3627 -> 35.4020, kL 66.1867 -> 66.9140, ISO 67.3680 -> 67.4113, CTL 35.2393 -> 35.3087; TRAIN 35.5227 -> 35.6293 / 99.2493 -> 99.8767 / 95.8907 -> 96.1573 / 35.4553 -> 35.5400. Paired per seed rho 1.0008 / 1.0012 / 0.9985. DELTA_ID @328 = ISO - CTL +32.1027 pp = +42.48 SE; ISO - kL @328 +0.4973 (+0.66 SE); NULL MODEL k01 @328 - @100 +0.0393 (+0.05 SE); kL 12/13/13 of 26 groups FREE. Every arm's seed range <= 0.564. All six registered point predictions landed IN band (rho [0.96,1.04], the four levels, and the pin bound). The re-registered freedom gate, graded: ISO's complement is PINNED on 3/3 by step-size MAGNITUDE (MED_R 1.0010 / 1.0020 / 1.0020, MAX_R 1.197 / 1.273 / 1.234) while cIS2's superseded exact-clamp-dwell rule scores 0.4195 / 0.3780 / 0.3610 and would have called it NOT PINNED -- the 196.5 defect, reproduced and removed -- and the gate sits AFTER the primary, so no RHO can be lost to it. Pin (r<=2) at epoch 104.8 / 106.4 / 107.8, post-pin window 220.2 ep >= W_MAX 213.0, and ISO's TEST over epochs 113-117 is 67.3433 against 67.4113 at the end: +0.0680 pp = +0.09 SE. Registered scorer run UNEDITED on alice2, exit 0, 105 PASS / 0 FAIL / 0 SKIP; an independent parser agrees digit for digit and re-grades the branch map to the same branch.

experiments.scope: cvh1, 12 runs, VGG11_bn_c100 / CIFAR-100, SGDm+Lion, ms 1e-3, alpha0 1e-6, box -15:-2.3026, AUGMENT=1, PROBE=100 + PROBE_TENSOR=1 on every arm (1,640 records/run), 328 ep, fresh seeds {63,64,65}; horizon E = ceil(PIN_BOUND 114.7865 + W_MAX 213.0) = 328 by the 190 method; ingest 2,884 -> 2,926 together with cuc1 (added 42, changed 0, removed 0); 17.32 GPU-h re-summed over its own 12 wallclock_min values (sacct 17.44). cvi1's HORIZON-100-ONLY bound is retired for this arm: the VGG rescue is unattenuated at 328 epochs, and the complement pinned inside cvi1's own extrapolated 109-113 window, so the 190 extrapolation method has now bounded a measured pin three times. But 'survives' means A LEVEL FROZEN AT THE PIN, NOT CONTINUED LEARNING (+0.0680 pp over 220 post-pin epochs; ISO-TRAIN-FROZEN says the same on TRAIN), and rho ~ 1 is not a bound -- 213's own floor gate predicts 1.00-1.07 under the NEVER-PINS account too, which is why the pin state is reported beside it. experiments.title: Does the denominator hold in the parent's own UNAUGMENTED setting on CIFAR-100 -- the two counts cau1 left open (CIFAR-100, and meta-side tuning beyond two alpha0 cells)?
experiments.goal: Does the denominator hold in the parent's own UNAUGMENTED setting on CIFAR-100 -- the two counts cau1 left open (CIFAR-100, and meta-side tuning beyond two alpha0 cells)?
experiments.comparison: AUGMENT=0 on EVERY arm: a 5-rung plain-SGD lr ladder (0.05 / 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.4 / 0.8, momentum 0.9, wd 5e-4, cosine COS_TOTAL=50000 COS_WARMUP=1000) against a 5-cell meta-stepsize x alpha0 plus-grid around the corpus-best augmented cell; one batch, one granularity

experiments.result: PRIMARY GAP_END = plateau5(S*) - plateau5(M*) = 65.0573 - 52.8793 = +12.1780 pp = +26.05 SE (SE 0.4674; the frozen prior 0.572475 dominates the in-batch 0.5555, df 18). THE LADDER IS INTERIOR -- 62.658 / 63.097 / 64.774 / 65.057 / 59.848, argmax the 4th of 5 rungs, falling 5.209 pp = 11.14 SE at the top -- so the token does NOT take | LOWER-BOUND. Grid: 48.457 / 52.749 / 52.879 / 47.057 / 14.195, the last DOES NOT TRAIN. M* is an EDGE cell (ms-HIGH) but beats the CENTRE by only +0.1307 pp = +0.28 SE, so the registered map gives plain DEFICIT-HOLDS with METHOD:FLAT-TOP-MS-HIGH, not DEFICIT-HOLDS-METHOD-EDGE. Every rung beats every cell (smallest margin lr08 - M* = +6.969 pp). PEAK +9.1087 pp = +25.37 SE_PEAK (endpoint and early-stopping AGREE); TUNING M* - REF +4.4220 pp = +9.46 SE (the augmented cell spec is genuinely mistuned here, and the gap is measured against the retuned cell); CURVE +6.9710 pp = +17.62 SE_CURVE at the best-AUC rung but -2.3489 pp at S*, hence CURVE-DEFICIT-LOWER-BOUND. TRAIN plateau5 >= 99.96 on every training arm (TRAIN-AUC gap -22.9231; epoch-to-99 % 18-19 for M* against 80 for S*). Selection: S* and M* are both max-of-5, worst-case bias ~0.384 pp EACH in OPPOSITE directions; adversely +11.41 pp = 24.4 SE. 214's disclosed adverse sensitivity model, which predicted every cell at 4-15 pp and a GATED-METHOD-AT-FLOOR non-answer, DID NOT FIRE: four of five cells train at 47.06-52.88 pp and only the alpha0-HIGH corner floors. RULE 20 at full 30/30 per family AND per cell, the separate ENV audit (AUGMENT=0 in the ENV line AND the NODE= header of all 30), the 30/30 SGD_* runtime /proc/environ witness (SGD_count=0 + positive control) and a build_optimizer.py sha256 and mtime re-check against PROVENANCE.txt all PASS before any number. experiments.title: On the residual-free ResNet-18, is layer4.1.bn2.weight's rescue the removal of its VOTE from the shared meta-gradient sum or its OWN STEP SIZE -- and does a vote act by its SIZE or by its OWNER?
experiments.goal: On the residual-free ResNet-18, is layer4.1.bn2.weight's rescue the removal of its VOTE from the shared meta-gradient sum or its OWN STEP SIZE -- and does a vote act by its SIZE or by its OWNER?
experiments.comparison: PlainNet18_c100 at cpl2's cell with PATCH_VOTEWEIGHT (VOTE_W=<tensor>:<w> multiplies one tensor's term inside the unnormalised shared sum, before the sign; proved inert bitwise before launch, 227.4): k01 scalar; HEAD {50} [52,1] (cpl2's HEAD, BYTE-IDENTICAL: the positive control); MUTE = scalar grouping with 50's term x0 (50 keeps the shared step size and stops voting); DOSE = the same x0.1; INJECT = HEAD's grouping with the twin 47 layer4.1.bn1.weight x691 (fixed K, sign kept) inside the complement; ONE batch

experiments.result: CO-PRIMARY P_VOTE = HEAD - MUTE = 64.7940 - 10.9860 = +53.8080 pp = +94.90 SE; CO-PRIMARY P_INJECT = HEAD - INJECT = 64.7940 - 30.1400 = +34.6540 pp = +61.12 SE (SE 0.5670, the frozen prior; in-batch 0.5959); TRAIN +68.7867 / +48.9500. KEY D_HEAD +52.8447 pp = +93.20 SE (positive control; cpl2 +52.3647, between-batch); D_MUTE -0.9633 pp = -1.70 SE; D_DOSE -0.0007 pp; D_INJ +18.1907 pp = +32.08 SE. Levels (TEST / TRAIN): k01 11.9493 / 11.85, HEAD 64.7940 / 79.72, MUTE 10.9860 / 10.94, DOSE 11.9487 / 12.06, INJECT 30.1400 / 30.77; every seed range <= 1.37 pp. G-BITE PASS on 15/15 (500 records each; intervened runs 457-485 informative records, unweighted-sum match on 0); an independent check adds that every interior beta step follows the WEIGHTED Lion direction, and on the 9-113 records per run where weighted and unweighted directions disagree it follows the weighted one on all and the unweighted on none. Pins: k01 36.2-36.6; MUTE 40.2-40.6; DOSE never continuously (at the clamp 0.12-0.19 of records, -14.96 to -15.00 at the end); INJECT's complement 37.6 on all seeds (HEAD's 99.8), its isolated 50 at 20.8-23.6 as HEAD's. experiments.reason: Verdict: STEP-SIZE-NEEDED-VOTE-SUFFICES + HARNESS-CLEAN + PATCH-BITES + K-FIXED-691 + ONE-NETWORK-PLAINNET + HORIZON-100-ONLY + SIGMA-PRIOR-FROZEN + POSITIVE-CONTROL-REPRODUCES + DOSE-AT-K01 + INJECT-PARTIAL + MUTE-BELOW-HEAD + FLOOR-READINGS-ARE-BOUNDS + TRAIN-AGREES Mixed: STEP-SIZE-NEEDED-VOTE-SUFFICES: muting layer4.1.bn2.weight's vote while it keeps the shared step size does not rescue (MUTE at k01), and a carrier-sized vote cast by its bn1 twin collapses HEAD's complement (P_INJECT +34.65 pp); but INJECT is a partial collapse (INJECT-PARTIAL) and misses its registered 8-30 band by 0.14 pp.
experiments.scope: cvt1, 15 runs, PlainNet18_c100 / CIFAR-100, SGDm+Lion, ms 1e-3, alpha0 1e-6, box -15:-2.3026, AUGMENT=1, PROBE=100 + PROBE_TENSOR=1, 100 ep, fresh seeds {78,79,80}; ingested alone (2,956 -> 2,971, added 15, changed 0); 10.22 GPU-h re-summed over its own 15 wallclock_min values (sacct 10.38). The 9 MUTE / DOSE / INJECT rows carry k01's / HEAD's CSV cell key (no VOTE_W column) and are listed in results/CORPUS-EXCLUSIONS.tsv; [SUPERSEDED, not true when written: every cell-pooling reader drops them.] [AMENDED at cycle 152, CORRECTIONS 231: no file in analysis/ imports analysis/corpus_exclusions.py, and at least one existing reader pools them -- cPL2_plainnet_head_score.py --selftest re-derives SIGMA_PLAIN on the live corpus as 8.6778 (df 24), against 0.4107 (df 15) with the 9 rows dropped; it prints a NOTE and feeds no bar (O2). The rule now reads: every FUTURE noise-floor or corpus-sigma derivation must drop them with corpus_exclusions.filter_rows first, and say so in its registration entry (docs/OPERATIONS.md, registration checklist); frozen-literal bars of already-registered scorers are unaffected.]. The first intervention on the vote itself, and it separates the two halves of isolation: silencing 50's vote while it keeps the shared step size does NOT rescue (MUTE at k01), so the rescue needs 50 on its own step size; and a carrier-sized vote cast by a DIFFERENT tensor into HEAD's rescued complement pins that complement within ~1.4 epochs of k01's pin (37.6 vs 36.2-36.6) and costs 34.65 pp, so a vote's collapsing effect is at least partly its SIZE, not only its owner. Bounded, and led with (230.4): INJECT is a PARTIAL collapse -- 18.19 pp (+32 SE) above k01, 0.344 of the HEAD gap kept, 0.14 pp above the top of the registered 8-30 band; the branch is bar-relative (P_INJECT 24.65 pp over COLLAPSE). NOT licensed: that magnitude alone collapses (INJECT stays well above k01), that identity is irrelevant, or which property of 50 needs the own step size; that x691 is minimal or record-matched (one K); any dose-response (one dose, and DOSE sits at k01 like MUTE, so it cannot separate threshold from graded); ResNet (BN or GN) or VGG; anything past 100 epochs; RULE 11.

experiments.title: Is the GroupNorm isolation rescue (cgn2, 225) a rescue or a delayed collapse that 100 epochs could not see -- and what happens to ONE's partial rescue?
experiments.goal: Is the GroupNorm isolation rescue (cgn2, 225) a rescue or a delayed collapse that 100 epochs could not see -- and what happens to ONE's partial rescue?
experiments.comparison: ResNet18_gn_c100 at cgn2's cell to E = 430 epochs, spec strings BYTE-IDENTICAL to cgn2's: k01 scalar, kL layerwise, ISO {50 layer4.0.bn2.weight, 53 layer4.0.shortcut.1.weight, 59 layer4.1.bn2.weight} [59,3], ONE {50} [61,1]; no CTL arm; the 100-epoch control read IN RUN from epochs 95-99 of the same runs (proved on the tree and the live train.py / HF.py before launch); ONE batch
experiments.why: Mechanism-hunt row in section 9's convention, appended at the file's end so that no existing line moves -- CORRECTIONS 231.
experiments.result: PRIMARY RHO = D_ISO@430 / D_ISO@100 = +48.5193 / +39.6573 = 1.2235 (D_ISO +62.34 SE at 430, +50.95 SE at 100; SE 0.7783, the frozen prior 0.9532 dominating the in-batch 0.7036); per-seed paired rho 1.2376 / 1.2035 / 1.2302; TRAIN RHO 1.6144 (+47.37 -> +76.48). Levels TEST @100 -> @430 (TRAIN @430): k01 14.4460 -> 14.8427 (16.93), kL 51.6100 -> 66.3853 (99.79), ISO 54.1033 -> 63.3620 (93.41), ONE 39.8920 -> 56.6187 (81.56); every seed range <= 2.93 pp. ONE: RHO_ONE 1.6418 (+25.4460 -> +41.7760), share of the kL gap 0.6847 -> 0.8105, ISO - ONE +14.21 -> +6.74. ISO - kL +2.49 at 100, -3.02 pp (-3.88 SE) at 430; kL passes ISO for good at epoch 174. Pin gate (step-size magnitude, last quarter): ISO's complement PINNED on 3/3 (median r 1.03 / 1.02 / 1.03), first r <= 2 at epoch 238.4 / 221.0 / 215.2 (inside the 335.5 bound), never re-freed (<= 0.4 % of later records above r 2); ONE's complement PINNED at 282.6 / 282.8 / 312.6; k01 PINNED at 195-219; the isolated groups on the clamp from epoch ~20. Post-pin: ISO TEST 63.34 at epochs 244-248 vs 63.36 at the end (+0.03 SE), per-seed OLS -0.05 to +0.03 pp per 100 epochs over 186-209 epochs; ONE -0.07 to +0.03 over 112-142. But ISO's TEST settled (within 0.5 pp of its end, for good) at epoch 162, while its complement r was still 49-76 -- 53-76 epochs BEFORE the pin -- and TRAIN kept rising (87.0 at 150 -> 93.0 at 225 -> 93.4). Registered scorer run UNEDITED on alice2, exit 0, 87 PASS / 0 FAIL; an independent parser reproduces every level, contrast, the branch and all 20 conditional stamps, byte-identical on alice2 and the Mac.
experiments.reason: Verdict: RESCUE-SURVIVES + RHO:1.2235 + TRAIN-AGREES + COMPLEMENT-PINNED + ISO-PIN-EPOCH:224.9 + POST-PIN-WINDOW:191.6 + WINDOW-MEETS-W100 + PIN-INSIDE-BOUND + FROZEN-AT-PIN + RHO-ONE:1.6418 + ONE-SURVIVES + ONE-SHARE-RISES + ONE-COMPLEMENT-PINNED + HEAD3-NARROWS + CEIL-BELOW + KL-STILL-TRAINING + K01-PINNED + FLOOR-HOLDS + ISO-TRAIN-MOVES + SIGMA-FROZEN-DOMINATES + DIFFERS-FROM-CGN2 + MAGNITUDE-NOT-SEPARATED + NO-IN-BATCH-CTL + GN32-ALSO-CHANGES-PER-CHANNEL-INVARIANCE + ONE-CELL-ONLY Goal met: RESCUE-SURVIVES: the GroupNorm isolation rescue holds to 430 epochs (RHO 1.2235) after its complement's step size pins, every arm lands in the tested FREEZE-HOLDS account's registered band, and ONE survives with a rising share of the kL gap (0.68 -> 0.81). Bounded: the level settled before the pin, and ISO ends 3.02 pp below kL (CEIL-BELOW).
experiments.scope: cgn3, 12 runs, ResNet18_gn_c100 / CIFAR-100, SGDm+Lion, ms 1e-3, alpha0 1e-6, box -15:-2.3026, AUGMENT=1, PROBE=100 + PROBE_TENSOR=1, 430 ep, fresh seeds {81,82,83}; ingested alone (2,971 -> 2,983, added 12, changed 0); 38.70 GPU-h re-summed over its own 12 wallclock_min values (sacct 38.81). These rows are 430-epoch measurements (epochs_done 430) and must not be pooled into a 100-epoch GN cell.. On GroupNorm the isolation rescue is a regime, not a delayed collapse: the complement's step size DOES pin (at ~225, inside the extrapolated bound, not in the never-pins tail 228 feared), and the rescued level holds flat for ~190 epochs after it, as on VGG (cvh1) and ResNet BN (ciso2). ONE's partial rescue is not partial at long horizon: 50 alone reaches 0.81 of the kL gap. Bounded, and led with: (1) the survival is of a LEVEL that stopped rising at ~162 -- before the pin, while TRAIN kept climbing -- so the plateau is not caused by the pin in time, and 'the pin freezes the level' is not licensed; (2) the rescued arm does NOT track the layerwise ceiling at long horizon: kL climbs on to 66.39 and ISO sits 3.02 pp below it (CEIL-BELOW), so 'isolating three tensors recovers layerwise' holds at 100 epochs only; (3) D_ISO@100 here is 1.96 pp below cgn2's (DIFFERS-FROM-CGN2, between-batch, descriptive). NOT licensed: persistence past 430 epochs or a decay slower than 1.56 pp per ~190 epochs; identity vs magnitude (MAGNITUDE-NOT-SEPARATED); DELTA_ID at 430 (no CTL arm); any other normaliser (GN(32) also changes per-channel invariance), network or cell; the mechanism of the pre-pin TEST plateau (UNSURE); RULE 11.

experiments.title: cvt1's MUTE failed while the DOWN vote moved to other BN scales: does silencing layer4.1.bn2.weight AND the whole DOWN coalition -- every tensor still on ONE shared step size -- rescue the scalar arm, or is the own step size needed after all?
experiments.goal: cvt1's MUTE failed while the DOWN vote moved to other BN scales: does silencing layer4.1.bn2.weight AND the whole DOWN coalition -- every tensor still on ONE shared step size -- rescue the scalar arm, or is the own step size needed after all?
experiments.comparison: PlainNet18_c100 at cvt1's cell, from cvt1's unchanged PATCH_VOTEWEIGHT tree (no new harness code): k01 scalar; HEAD {50} [52,1] (BYTE-IDENTICAL to cvt1/cpl2: the positive control); MUTE50 = scalar with 50's term x0 (cvt1's MUTE, replicated); MUTEDOWN = scalar with {50} + RULE C's 20-tensor DOWN coalition x0 (47 44 41 38 35 32 29 26 23 20 17 14 40 46 43 11 37 8 5 49: 15 BN scales + 5 convs, 0.828 of the vote mass on cvt1 MUTE's post-epoch-36 records); MUTECTL = scalar with {50} + RULE K's count- and class-matched NON-DOWN set x0 (15 BN biases of the same modules + 5 smaller convs, 0.028 of the mass, NOT mass-matched); G-RUNAWAY registered against an UP-runaway; ONE batch
experiments.why: Mechanism-hunt row in section 9's convention, appended at the file's end so that no existing line moves -- CORRECTIONS 235.
experiments.result: PRIMARY P_COAL = MUTEDOWN - MUTECTL = 11.3293 - 7.8213 = +3.5080 pp = +6.19 SE (SE 0.5670, the frozen prior; in-batch 0.4309); TRAIN +3.5593. KEY D_DOWN -0.2427 pp = -0.43 SE; D_CTL -3.7507 pp = -6.61 SE; D_MUTE50 -0.2773 pp; D_HEAD +53.0240 pp = +93.52 SE; G_DOWN +53.2667 pp. Levels (TEST / TRAIN): k01 11.5720 / 11.65, HEAD 64.5960 / 79.25, MUTE50 11.2947 / 11.17, MUTEDOWN 11.3293 / 11.29, MUTECTL 7.8213 / 7.73; every seed range <= 1.38 pp. G-BITE + G-BITE-SET PASS on 15/15 (intervened runs 453-500 informative records, unweighted match 0; MUTEDOWN / MUTECTL 320-497 set-informative records, 50-only and other-set match 0); every interior beta step follows the WEIGHTED Lion direction, and on the 10-34 records per run where weighted and unweighted directions disagree it follows the weighted one on all. G-RUNAWAY: 0 of 15 runs (0.000 of post-epoch-17 records at the ceiling; highest shared beta -4.110, MUTECTL). Shared-beta pins: k01 36.4; MUTE50 40.2-40.6; MUTECTL 41.2-41.4; MUTEDOWN at or below -14 from epoch 40.4-43.0 on 0.95-0.99 of later records (continuous pin only at 90.6-99.6); HEAD's complement 96.4-99.8. On MUTEDOWN's post-epoch-36 records the sum votes DOWN on 0.91-0.99 of records, re-carried by convs 28, 16, 25 and bn1.weight (0.55-0.60 of the weighted mass DOWN outside the coalition). Registered scorer run UNEDITED on alice2, exit 0; an independent parser agrees on every level, contrast, the runaway gate, branch and stamp
experiments.reason: Verdict: OWN-STEP-NECESSARY + HARNESS-CLEAN + PATCH-BITES + SETS-FROM-CVT1-MUTE + CTL-COUNT-CLASS-NOT-MASS + NO-TIME-GATE + ONE-NETWORK-PLAINNET + HORIZON-100-ONLY + SIGMA-PRIOR-FROZEN + POSITIVE-CONTROL-REPRODUCES + MUTE50-AT-K01 + CTL-BELOW-K01 + FLOOR-READINGS-ARE-BOUNDS + TRAIN-AGREES Mixed: OWN-STEP-NECESSARY: silencing layer4.1.bn2.weight and the whole 20-tensor DOWN coalition, with every tensor on one shared step size, leaves the scalar arm at k01 (MUTEDOWN 11.33 vs k01 11.57), which strengthens MT218's 'the rescue needs 50 on its own step size'; but the account misses its registered MUTECTL band by 0.18 pp, P_COAL (+3.51 pp) comes from the control falling below k01 rather than from the coalition (MUTEDOWN - MUTE50 +0.03 pp), and the DOWN vote was re-carried by the next tier, so 'no silenced set rescues' is not licensed.
experiments.scope: cvt3, 15 runs, PlainNet18_c100 / CIFAR-100, SGDm+Lion, ms 1e-3, alpha0 1e-6, box -15:-2.3026, AUGMENT=1, PROBE=100 + PROBE_TENSOR=1, 100 ep, fresh seeds {84,85,86}; ingested with cvt2 (2,983 -> 3,019, added 36, changed 0); 9.92 GPU-h re-summed over its own 15 wallclock_min values (sacct 10.11). The 9 MUTE50 / MUTEDOWN / MUTECTL rows carry k01's CSV cell key and are listed in results/CORPUS-EXCLUSIONS.tsv (corpus_exclusions.py --check PASS). Silencing the whole DOWN coalition while every tensor shares the step size does not rescue: cvt1's 'the rescue needs 50 on its own step size' survives the re-carriage objection at the coalition level (STRENGTHENED, as registered). The OWN-STEP-NECESSARY account hits 5 of its 6 predictions (MUTECTL misses its 8-16 band by 0.18 pp, below); COALITION and NONSPECIFIC miss MUTEDOWN / MUTECTL by >= 44 pp. Bounded, and led with (235.4): (1) the vote was re-carried AGAIN by the next tier the eligibility bar left in, so 'no silenced set rescues' is NOT licensed; (2) P_COAL is positive only because the control fell 3.75 pp BELOW k01 (MUTEDOWN - MUTE50 = +0.03 pp), and why is UNSURE; (3) descriptive, UNSURE: every scalar arm's shared step size over epochs 15-30 was LARGER than HEAD's complement's (10,749-13,845 vs 8,672 x the floor) and TEST settled by epoch 21-25 while it was still large, so the scalar arms do not fail for want of shared step size in the window where the level is set. NOT licensed: that no other silenced set rescues; WHY the own step size is needed; a mass-matched control; any time-gated silence; ResNet (BN or GN) or VGG; anything past 100 epochs; RULE 11.

experiments.title: Is cvt1's injected collapse of HEAD's complement a THRESHOLD or GRADED in the twin's weight K, and was the 0.344 residue a matter of dose?
experiments.goal: Is cvt1's injected collapse of HEAD's complement a THRESHOLD or GRADED in the twin's weight K, and was the 0.344 residue a matter of dose?
experiments.comparison: PlainNet18_c100 at cvt1's cell, from cvt1's unchanged PATCH_VOTEWEIGHT tree (no new harness code): k01 scalar; HEAD {50} [52,1] (K = 1, BYTE-IDENTICAL to cvt1/cpl2); HEAD's grouping with layer4.1.bn1.weight (idx 47) x K inside the complement at K = 13, 33 (the 'initiate-but-not-sustain' interval in log thirds), 152, 691 (cvt1's INJECT byte for byte) and 2000; K derived from cvt1's probe records (233.3); no time gate (dose and onset confounded, disclosed); ONE batch
experiments.why: Mechanism-hunt row in section 9's convention, appended at the file's end so that no existing line moves -- CORRECTIONS 236.
experiments.result: PRIMARY SHAPE from K13 / K33 / K152 against HEAD and K691: HEAD - K13 = +12.0693 pp, K13 - K691 = +22.0720 (BETWEEN); HEAD - K33 = +28.8253, K33 - K691 = +5.3160 (BETWEEN, 0.32 pp outside MATCH); HEAD - K152 = +30.0767, K152 - K691 = +4.0647 (AT-PLATEAU). PRIMARY TOP = K691 - K2000 = +5.2593 pp = +7.39 SE (SE 0.7121, in-batch sigma 0.8721 over the 0.6944 prior); TRAIN +5.8187. D_HEAD +52.9420 pp = +74.35 SE; P691 = HEAD - K691 = +34.1413 pp. Levels (TEST / TRAIN): k01 11.4767 / 11.29, HEAD 64.4187 / 78.83, K13 52.3493 / 62.02, K33 35.5933 / 36.87, K152 34.3420 / 35.38, K691 30.2773 / 30.89, K2000 25.0180 / 25.07; share of the HEAD gap kept 0.772 / 0.456 / 0.432 / 0.355 / 0.256; every seed range <= 2.80 pp. G-BITE PASS on 21/21 (ladder runs 408-498 informative records, unweighted match 0; every interior step follows the weighted Lion direction, on 90-236 disagreeing records per ladder run). Complement pins: HEAD 99.6-99.8; K13 never (still descending, arm mean -12.16 at epoch 100; TEST still rising +0.015 to +0.028 pp per epoch); K33 at or below -14 from 36.4-37.8 (continuous pin 38.4 / 85.8 / 97.4); K152 38.2-38.4; K691 37.6-37.8; K2000 36.8-37.0. DOM epoch HEAD 44.2-49.8, K13 20.0 / 89.0 / never, K33 18.2-18.6, K152 17.0-17.2, K691 16.6-16.8, K2000 16.2-16.4. Registered scorer run UNEDITED on alice2, exit 0; an independent parser agrees on every level, contrast, shape state, TOP token and stamp
experiments.reason: Verdict: GRADED + TOP-ATTENUATED + HARNESS-CLEAN + PATCH-BITES + ONE-NETWORK-PLAINNET + HORIZON-100-ONLY + DOSE-ONSET-CONFOUNDED + SIGMA-INBATCH + POSITIVE-CONTROL-REPRODUCES + K13-BETWEEN + K33-BETWEEN + K152-AT-PLATEAU + TRAIN-AGREES Mixed: GRADED + TOP-ATTENUATED: the twin's injected vote collapses HEAD's complement by degree in K (share of the HEAD gap kept 0.772 at K13 down to 0.256 at K2000), so cvt1's 0.344 residue is not a fixed floor; but no registered account predicted this pair of words, the stated TOP-FLAT prior missed by 0.26 pp, both words sit on near bars (K33 0.32 pp and TOP 0.26 pp past the 5.0 pp bar), and K13 is still rising at 100 epochs, so its level may be a delay.
experiments.scope: cvt2, 21 runs, PlainNet18_c100 / CIFAR-100, SGDm+Lion, ms 1e-3, alpha0 1e-6, box -15:-2.3026, AUGMENT=1, PROBE=100 + PROBE_TENSOR=1, 100 ep, fresh seeds {87,88,89}; ingested with cvt3 (2,983 -> 3,019, added 36, changed 0); 15.68 GPU-h re-summed over its own 21 wallclock_min values (sacct 15.90). The 15 K13-K2000 rows carry HEAD's CSV cell key and are listed in results/CORPUS-EXCLUSIONS.tsv (corpus_exclusions.py --check PASS). The injected collapse is graded in K, and cvt1's 0.344 residue is not a fixed floor: it falls to 0.256 at K2000. cvt1's INJECT replicates (K691 30.28 vs 30.14, between batch). No registered account returns this pair of words exactly: SIGN-SAT-GRADED and KNEE-AT-INITIATION hit 6 of 7 levels (K33 below its band by 2.41 pp; K13 above by 14.35), and the registered prior TOP-FLAT missed by 0.26 pp. Bounded, and led with (236.4): (1) both words sit on near bars (K33 0.32 pp and TOP 0.26 pp past MATCH), so GRADED rests on K13 alone, and K13 is still rising with an unpinned complement at 100 epochs -- its level may be a delay; (2) the sign-saturation derivation failed at K33: on each arm's own records the K needed to hold the collapse scales with K (median 12.9 at K13, 26-30 at K33, 78-96 at K691, 197-279 at K2000), so K33 held on 0.92-1.00 of its records; (3) from K33 up the complement's beta falls at Lion's maximum rate on every arm and the rungs differ by ONSET (first beta <= -8 at epoch 24.4 / 23.6-23.8 / 22.8-23.0 for K152 / K691 / K2000), so the dose effect above 152 is consistent with onset bought by dose (confounded, UNSURE); level ranks with the complement's step-size multiplier over epochs 15-30 (Spearman 0.965, descriptive). NOT licensed: a functional form or knee location; that the grading is a vote equilibrium; separating dose from onset; any caster but the twin; ResNet (BN or GN) or VGG; anything past 100 epochs; RULE 11.

experiments.title: With layer4.1.bn2.weight's vote already out of the complement's sum (HEAD's grouping), is the MAGNITUDE of its own step size the lever: does a large step size on 50 stall the network, and does a small one keep the rescue?
experiments.goal: With layer4.1.bn2.weight's vote already out of the complement's sum (HEAD's grouping), is the MAGNITUDE of its own step size the lever: does a large step size on 50 stall the network, and does a small one keep the rescue?
experiments.comparison: PlainNet18_c100 at cvt1's cell, from an isolated tree = cvt1's + the additive, opt-in PATCH_BETAHOLD (overwrites one group's beta after every meta update and its clamp, and at init; the held group's momentum is dead state): k01 scalar; HEAD {50} [52,1] (BYTE-IDENTICAL: the positive control); HOLDLOW (50's beta at the -15 floor from init); HOLDSHARED (50's beta := the complement's live beta; cvt1's MUTE in exact arithmetic); HOLDHIGH (exogenous max-rate replay of MUTE's measured shared trajectory, tri:9428: peak -4.39 at epoch 18.9, clamp at 40.1); HOLDHEAD (replay of HEAD's own median 50-trajectory, tri:5041: the hold's positive control); no time gate; ONE batch
experiments.why: Mechanism-hunt row in section 9's convention, appended at the file's end so that no existing line moves -- CORRECTIONS 240.
experiments.result: CO-PRIMARY P_HIGH = HEAD - HOLDHIGH = 64.7347 - 11.1267 = +53.6080 pp = +94.55 SE (TRAIN +68.8720; per seed +54.00 / +53.24 / +53.59); P_COUP = HOLDHIGH - HOLDSHARED = -0.2673 pp = -0.47 SE (TRAIN -0.1633); P_LOW = HOLDLOW - HEAD = +0.7260 pp = +1.28 SE (TRAIN +1.5193; per seed +0.92 / +1.14 / +0.12) (SE 0.5670, the frozen prior; in-batch 0.4638). KEY D_HEAD +53.0400 pp = +93.54 SE; P_CTL = HEAD - HOLDHEAD +0.0687 pp = +0.12 SE. Levels (TEST / TRAIN): k01 11.6947 / 11.51, HEAD 64.7347 / 79.99, HOLDLOW 65.4607 / 81.51, HOLDSHARED 11.3940 / 11.28, HOLDHIGH 11.1267 / 11.12, HOLDHEAD 64.6660 / 79.25; every seed range <= 1.22 pp. State margins: HOLDLOW 5.73 pp and HOLDHEAD 4.93 pp inside AT-HEAD; HOLDSHARED 2.30 pp and HOLDHIGH 2.57 pp inside AT-K01. G-BITE PASS on 18/18 (500 records each; every unheld group equals Lion recomputed, 0 mismatches, worst 4.0e-07; the held group on its schedule at every record in both beta and beta_pre; the patch's own bh_* record audits; no bh_* key on k01 / HEAD); read against any other hold mode, every run fails on 101-398 records. Complement pins: HEAD 97.8-99.6; HOLDLOW 99.6 / never; HOLDSHARED and HOLDHIGH 40.2-40.4 (MUTE's path, within 0.06-0.16 of the replay); HEAD's own 50 pins at 20.2-22.8. Registered scorer run UNEDITED on alice2, exit 0; an independent parser rebuilds 154/154 of its lines verbatim
experiments.reason: Verdict: OWN-STEP-MAGNITUDE + HARNESS-CLEAN + PATCH-BITES + HOLD-FROM-INIT + REPLAY-MAX-RATE-TRIANGLE + SHARED-IS-MUTE-ARITHMETIC + ONE-NETWORK-PLAINNET + HORIZON-100-ONLY + SIGMA-PRIOR-FROZEN + POSITIVE-CONTROL-REPRODUCES + HOLDLOW-AT-HEAD + HOLDSHARED-AT-K01 + HOLDHIGH-AT-K01 + HOLDHEAD-AT-HEAD + FLOOR-READINGS-ARE-BOUNDS + TRAIN-AGREES Goal met: OWN-STEP-MAGNITUDE: with layer4.1.bn2.weight's vote out of the complement's sum in every held arm, its own step size held large (HOLDHIGH, MUTE's measured trajectory replayed) stalls the arm at k01 (11.13 vs k01 11.69) and held at the floor from init keeps HEAD's level (HOLDLOW 65.46 vs HEAD 64.73); P_HIGH +53.61 pp = +94.55 SE, the registered account hits all 9 of its bands, and the replayed HEAD trajectory reproduces HEAD (P_CTL +0.07 pp). Bounded: HOLDHIGH's unforced complement collapsed too (pinned at epoch 40.4, HEAD's at 97.8-99.6), so a direct stall is not separated from one through the complement, and there is no time gate or dose curve.
experiments.scope: cvt4, 18 runs, PlainNet18_c100 / CIFAR-100, SGDm+Lion, ms 1e-3, alpha0 1e-6, box -15:-2.3026, AUGMENT=1, PROBE=100 + PROBE_TENSOR=1, 100 ep, fresh seeds {90,91,92}; ingested with cvt5 (3,019 -> 3,049, added 30, changed 0); 14.77 GPU-h re-summed over its own 18 wallclock_min values (sacct 14.96; four [HOST_3c1b003035] runs took 4,941-5,334 s). The 12 HOLDLOW / HOLDSHARED / HOLDHIGH / HOLDHEAD rows carry HEAD's CSV cell key and are listed in results/CORPUS-EXCLUSIONS.tsv with their BETA_HOLD witness (corpus_exclusions.py --check PASS, completeness 51/51). Confirmed by intervention, as registered: with its vote out of the complement's sum either way, 50 on a large step size (MUTE's trajectory, replayed) stalls the arm at k01, and 50 frozen at the floor keeps HEAD's level; cvt1's 'the rescue needs 50 on its own step size' sharpens to 'on a SMALL step size'. [AMENDED at cycle 152, CORRECTIONS 244: read as SUFFICIENCY at this cell -- the one large trajectory tested (MUTE's, replayed) is sufficient to stall, and 50 at the floor or on HEAD's own trajectory is sufficient to keep the rescue; no dose curve and no time window, so 'on a SMALL step size' says no more than that.] OWN-STEP-MAGNITUDE hits all 9 of its registered bands; the next-closest account (OWN-STEP-GRADED) misses HOLDHIGH by 8.87 pp. Bounded, and led with (240.4): (1) 'complement free' is not 'complement like HEAD's' -- in HOLDHIGH the unforced complement followed MUTE's collapse path and pinned at 40.4 (HEAD 97.8-99.6), so the batch cannot say whether 50's large step size stalls the network directly or through the complement's early collapse; descriptive, UNSURE: the TEST gap is already +2.05 pp after 17 epochs while the two complements' beta differ by 0.001 (by > 0.1 only from epoch 18.0-18.2), so the stall begins before the complements part; (2) no time gate and one shape per arm, so which window of the trajectory does the damage, and any dose curve, are untested; (3) the floor readings are locations [AMENDED at cycle 152, CORRECTIONS 244: so P_COUP ~ 0 (-0.27 pp) is a reading between two arms at the same floor location, not a measured absence of coupling; against COUPLING the batch says only that its predicted HOLDHIGH band 56-72 was missed, by 44.87 pp], and P_LOW (+0.73 pp, not a registered effect) speaks only to the first ~22 epochs, after which HEAD's own 50 is at the floor too. NOT licensed: that the stall is direct rather than via the complement; which window matters; a dose curve; why a large step size on this BN scale stalls; that HOLDSHARED and MUTE are the same run; any other tensor, network or horizon; RULE 11.

experiments.title: Does PlainNet's HEAD rescue survive 300 epochs past its own complement's pin, and is cvt2's GRADED (K13 between HEAD and the plateau at 100 epochs, still rising, complement unpinned) a delay or a K-dependent level?
experiments.goal: Does PlainNet's HEAD rescue survive 300 epochs past its own complement's pin, and is cvt2's GRADED (K13 between HEAD and the plateau at 100 epochs, still rising, complement unpinned) a delay or a K-dependent level?
experiments.comparison: PlainNet18_c100 at cvt1's cell, from cvt1's unchanged PATCH_VOTEWEIGHT tree (no new harness code), --num-epochs 300 with the 100-epoch control read in run: k01 scalar; HEAD {50} [52,1]; K13 and K33 (HEAD's grouping with layer4.1.bn1.weight x13 / x33 in the complement, cvt2's strings byte for byte); E = 300 derived from cvt2's K13 records (latest predicted r <= 2 at 223.5); pin gate by step-size MAGNITUDE (median r = exp(beta+15) over the last quarter of records), read as stamps after the branches; no time gate; ONE batch
experiments.why: Mechanism-hunt row in section 9's convention, appended at the file's end so that no existing line moves -- CORRECTIONS 241.
experiments.result: PRIMARY (a) G13 = K13@300 - K33@300 = 53.0807 - 37.1347 = +15.9460 pp = +23.04 SE (TRAIN +25.7233; +15.7167 at 100); DROP13 = K13@300 - K13@100 = +0.4193 pp = +0.61 SE (TRAIN +1.5847; per seed +0.45 / +0.48 / +0.33). PRIMARY (b) RHO = D_HEAD@300 / D_HEAD@100 = 52.6447 / 52.5807 = 1.0012 (TRAIN 1.0043; per seed 0.9995 / 1.0050 / 0.9992) (SE 0.6920, the frozen prior 0.8475; in-batch 0.6684). Levels at 100 / 300 (TEST; TRAIN at 300): k01 11.6280 / 11.6700 (11.67), HEAD 64.2087 / 64.3147 (78.87), K13 52.6613 / 53.0807 (64.15), K33 36.9447 / 37.1347 (38.43); every seed range <= 1.77 pp at either horizon. G-BITE PASS on 12/12 (1,500 records each; K13 / K33 1,409-1,414 informative records, unweighted match 0; every interior step follows the weighted Lion direction, including the 88-723 records per K run where weighted and unweighted disagree). Pin gate, first r <= 2: k01 34.8-35.0; HEAD 62.2-64.0 (0 records above r 2 after; at the exact clamp on 0.71-0.79 of them); K13 159.2-161.4 (median r 1.51 / 1.62 / 1.22, but back above r 2 on 74 / 104 / 5 later records; s94 ends at r 2.59); K33 37.0-69.4 (max r after epoch 100 1.23). K13's arm-mean TEST within 0.5 pp of its end from epoch 105. Registered scorer run UNEDITED on alice2, exit 0; an independent parser rebuilds 115/115 of its printed lines and the 32-token FINAL byte for byte
experiments.reason: Verdict: K-DEPENDENT-EQUILIBRIUM + RESCUE-SURVIVES + K33-HOLDS-PINNED + HARNESS-CLEAN + PATCH-BITES + ONE-NETWORK-PLAINNET + HORIZON-300 + NO-TIME-GATE + ONE-CELL-ONLY + SIGMA-PRIOR-FROZEN + RHO:1.0012 + TRAIN-AGREES-A + TRAIN-AGREES-B + K13-LEVEL-HOLDS + HEAD-LEVEL-HOLDS + K33-LEVEL-HOLDS + K13-COMPLEMENT-PINNED + K13-PIN-EPOCH:160.3 + K13-POST-PIN-WINDOW:138.6 + K13-WINDOW-MEETS-W100 + K13-PIN-INSIDE-BOUND + K13-FROZEN-AT-PIN + HEAD-COMPLEMENT-PINNED + HEAD-PIN-EPOCH:63.3 + HEAD-POST-PIN-WINDOW:236.0 + HEAD-WINDOW-MEETS-W100 + HEAD-FROZEN-AT-PIN + K33-COMPLEMENT-PINNED + K33-MAXR-POST100:1.2325 + K33-EXACT-CLAMP-CONTINUOUS + K01-PINNED + FLOOR-HOLDS Goal met: K-DEPENDENT-EQUILIBRIUM + RESCUE-SURVIVES + K33-HOLDS-PINNED: at 300 epochs K13 holds 15.95 pp above K33 (+23.04 SE) and moved +0.42 pp from its own 100-epoch level, so cvt2's GRADED (MT221) is not a delay; HEAD's PlainNet rescue survives its complement's magnitude pin (RHO 1.0012, level frozen for 236 post-pin epochs); K33 stays pinned; the tested EQUILIBRIUM + FREEZE-HOLDS account hits all 8 registered bands and no branch bar is near. Bounded: the level-holds and frozen-at-pin stamps sit only 0.96-1.34 pp inside READ_BAR, K13's step size hovers near the floor rather than freezing, and its level settled (epoch 105) before its pin (~160).
experiments.scope: cvt5, 12 runs, PlainNet18_c100 / CIFAR-100, SGDm+Lion, ms 1e-3, alpha0 1e-6, box -15:-2.3026, AUGMENT=1, PROBE=100 + PROBE_TENSOR=1, 300 ep, fresh seeds {93,94,95}; ingested with cvt4 (3,019 -> 3,049, added 30, changed 0); 25.03 GPU-h re-summed over its own 12 wallclock_min values (sacct 25.15). The 6 K13 / K33 rows carry HEAD's CSV cell key and are listed in results/CORPUS-EXCLUSIONS.tsv (corpus_exclusions.py --check PASS); k01 / HEAD are ordinary 300-epoch rows, kept out of 100-epoch cells by epochs_requested. [LED WITH THE BOUND, AMENDED at cycle 152, CORRECTIONS 244: no branch bar within 4.5 pp (closest DROP13, 4.58 pp); the stamps are soft (every level-holds and frozen-at-pin stamp 0.96-1.34 pp inside READ_BAR 1.384); K13's 'pinned' is a hover of the median r over the last quarter near the floor, not a clamp. K-DEPENDENT-EQUILIBRIUM is an equilibrium of the LEVEL only, with 231.4(1)'s qualifier: K13's TEST settled from ~epoch 105 and its complement first reached r <= 2 ~55 epochs later (159.2-161.4).] (a) cvt2's GRADED is NOT a delay at 300 epochs: K13 holds 15.95 pp above K33 and moved +0.42 pp from its in-run 100-epoch level, so the partial level is K-dependent. (b) PlainNet's HEAD rescue survives: RHO 1.0012, the level frozen for the 236 epochs after its complement's magnitude pin -- cvh1's / cgn3's sentence on a fourth network. (c) K33 stays pinned. EQUILIBRIUM + FREEZE-HOLDS hits all 8 registered bands; every other account misses at least one band by >= 6.92 pp. Bounded, and led with (241.4): (1) no branch bar is near (closest: DROP13 4.58 pp under +5), but every level-holds and frozen-at-pin stamp sits only 0.96-1.34 pp inside READ_BAR 1.384 -- locations, not tight nulls; (2) K13's 'pinned' is a median hovering near the floor, not a clamp: arm-mean beta rises -14.95 -> -14.54 over epochs 200-299, s94's complement ends above r 2, and the DOWN fraction stays near 0.5 -- its step size is small, not frozen; (3) the level stopped moving before the pin (settled at 105, first r <= 2 at ~160, TRAIN rising to ~160), so K13-FROZEN-AT-PIN is true as registered but 'the pin froze the level' is not licensed. The scorer's printed RESCUE-SURVIVES licence says the exact clamp came 'at ~96-100'; in this batch HEAD's exact-clamp dwell starts at 299.8 / never / 299.8 (registered text, not edited; no token reads it). NOT licensed: anything past 300 epochs; any K but 13 and 33 at long horizon; that K13's step size is frozen; dose vs onset; the ceiling (no kL); ResNet (BN or GN) or VGG; RULE 11.

But no registered account fits every band: GRADED's own account hits 3 of 5 (HIGHHEADPATH misses 20-50 by 8.51 pp, P_50 misses by 1.53 pp), as do DIRECT and EITHER-SUFFICES, so the pattern is a GRADED sub-case no account predicted. The 15 HOLDLOW / HOLDHIGH / HIGHHEADPATH / LOWMUTEPATH / LOWHEADPATH rows carry HEAD's CSV cell key and are listed in results/CORPUS-EXCLUSIONS.tsv with their BETA_HOLD witness; the 9 forced rows' COMP_HOLD line is verified through MULTI_KIND (corpus_exclusions.py --check PASS, completeness 75/75, two-kind 9/9). Bounded, and led with (246.4): no bar is near; the forced arms are open-loop, so whether the complement's lost responsiveness contributes when 50 is HIGH is untested (242.9); one shape per factor, no dose curve, no time gate (MUTEPATH and HEADPATH identical to 0.04 through epoch 18, one crossing at 22.45); readings at k01 are locations. Partly resolved, as registered (GRADED: no single-route sentence). Stamped states: HIGHHEADPATH (50 on MUTE's replay, complement forced open-loop onto HEADPATH) sits at the k01 location -- at this cell this one large 50 trajectory is sufficient to put the arm there with the complement on HEAD's measured path, which collapses late (r <= 2 from epoch 64.8) rather than on MUTE's early schedule; LOWMUTEPATH (50 at the floor, complement forced onto MUTEPATH) sits BETWEEN at 41.56 -- this one complement path is sufficient for a partial loss (P_C +23.47 pp) and does not reach the k01 location; the complement-hold control LOWHEADPATH keeps HEAD's level and cvt4's HOLDLOW / HOLDHIGH replicate at new seeds. 240.4(1)'s bound is PARTLY RESOLVED; neither state is a statement about necessity. No account's bands all fit (GRADED, DIRECT and EITHER-SUFFICES 3/5 each). Descriptive, UNSURE: HIGHHEADPATH departs from LOWHEADPATH at epoch line 16 with bitwise-identical complement schedules (as cvt4's split at 16); LOWMUTEPATH leads LOWHEADPATH by 1.1-2.2 pp at lines 22-24 and stays > 2 pp below only from line 28. P_INT +23.59 pp and R_LOW +0.71 pp are descriptive. NOT licensed: any single-route sentence; necessity; that the open-loop arms stand for closed-loop ones; which window matters; a dose curve; any other complement path; why a large step size on this BN scale stalls; any other tensor, network or horizon; RULE 11.

experiments.scope: cvt7, 15 runs, ResNet18_c100 / CIFAR-100, SGDm+Lion, ms 1e-3, alpha0 1e-6, box -15:-2.3026, AUGMENT=1, PROBE=100 + PROBE_TENSOR=1, 100 ep, fresh seeds {99,100,101}; ingested with cvt6 (3,049 -> 3,085, added 36, changed 0); 13.73 GPU-h re-summed over its own 15 wallclock_min values (sacct 13.86; four [HOST_3c1b003035] runs took 5,229-5,650 s). The 9 HOLDLOW / HOLDHIGH / HOLDISO rows carry ISO's CSV cell key and are listed in results/CORPUS-EXCLUSIONS.tsv with their GROUP_HOLD witness (corpus_exclusions.py --check PASS, completeness 75/75); with them in, the ResNet noise floor now depends on the filter (SIGMA_R18ALL 0.688153 filtered vs 2.208672 naive). Bounded, and led with (247.4): (1) dose and held set are confounded with network -- the one large trajectory is k01's own (peak -5.21 vs PlainNet's HOLDHIGH -4.39) and ResNet held three carriers together where PlainNet held idx 50 alone, so 'part on ResNet, all on PlainNet' is not attributable to the network; (2) the free complement did not stay ISO-like (magnitude pin 52.8-54.0 vs ISO's 92.6-99.4), so P_HIGH moves both and direct vs via-complement is not separated; (3) no bar is near (HOLDHIGH 14.81 pp under AT-ISO; the narrowest margins are HOLDISO +5.02 and HOLDLOW +5.26 pp inside AT-ISO). Partly transfers, as registered: at this cell this replay (k01's own trajectory, peak -5.21) on the carrier group is sufficient to cost ~20 pp of ISO's 47 pp rescue and is not sufficient to bring the run down to k01 (larger trajectories were not tested); the floor and ISO's own trajectory keep the rescue, so the hold does not break it by itself. TRANSFERS-GRADED hits every registered band; DOES-NOT-TRANSFER (= the broken-patch null) misses HOLDHIGH by 11.77 pp and is excluded by G-BITE too. P_LOW (+0.26 pp) is not an effect and speaks only to ~the first 23 epochs. Descriptive, UNSURE: the arm-mean TEST gap to ISO passes 2 pp at epoch line 16 while the two complements are identical to 0.000 (true on 2 of 3 seeds; s99 passes at line 17, just after its complements part); HOLDHIGH's TEST stays within 0.06 pp of k01's through line 16, dips 1.26-1.90 pp below at lines 17-18 and rises above from line 19. NOT licensed: necessity; any single carrier; which epochs matter; direct vs via the complement's earlier collapse; that ResNet is intrinsically less sensitive than PlainNet; a dose curve; any other network (GN, VGG), cell or horizon; RULE 11.
